layout: Golden vectors for FleetRing token spec v1 (docs/spec/tokens-v1.md). The file is append-only: new cases go at the end of their section, and existing cases never change (tokens-v1.lock freezes them). A change to any case's expected result is a new spec version and, where apply decides with it, a fleet feature (ADR-0047 point 6.5).

Results: a case that is accepted carries what the implementation returns; a refused case carries an error object. An error object has a kind, "error" or "violation", in snake_case, and the fields its variant names.

scope_texts: the scope grammar (spec section 2). text parses to scope, either "fleet" or {action, exact} or {action, prefix}, and prints back as canonical, which is always text; or it is refused with error shape, unknown_action, or empty_pattern.
pattern_matches: whether the pattern of a scope (the text after its first ':') matches the database name, byte for byte (spec section 2.2).
scope_sets: the canonical form of a set of scopes (spec section 3.3): sorted by text, with every scope another one covers dropped. A set is canonical exactly when it equals its canonical form.
action_meets: the meet of two actions (spec section 3.1), the strongest action both cover, or null. The meet is symmetric; each unordered pair appears once.
covers: whether the held scope covers the wanted scope (spec section 3.2).
meets: the meet of two scopes (spec section 3.2), or null when they share nothing.

narrowing: operation intersect gives result, a canonical list (spec section 3.4). operation grant_step gives result, a canonical list or an error no_grant or empty, and strict, the strict grant step's canonical list or an error no_grant, empty, or not_covered naming a scope (spec section 3.5). The first rows are ADR-0044 section 2.4's table, as written.
agent_names: an accepted name with its depth, root, and parent (null for a root agent), or an error principal, not_agent, segment, or too_deep (spec section 4).
at_or_below: whether name is at or below ancestor (spec section 4.2).

tier: the agent tier check (spec section 7.2) of scopes, in the order given, for agent: "ok", or the violation not_delegated, fleet, outside_root, grant_outside_child, or no_separator, the last three naming the first scope that breaks a rule.
claims_bases: named TokenClaims in the control state's JSON form (spec section 6.4), which issuer_signed_claims cases patch.

issuer_signed_claims: base patched with patch by JSON merge patch (RFC 7386: a null removes a field), then checked by the structural check of nodes (issuer_signed, spec section 7.1) and of apply and the signer (recordable, spec section 7.3). Each is "ok" or the violation not_delegated, not_agent, parent, chain_length {links, depth}, tier {tier: a tier violation}, no_issued_at, issued_after_start, ends_before_start, too_long, or starts_too_late.
delegation_ids: text is the delegation ID of the 16 bytes in lowercase hex, or is refused; token_id says whether a refused text is still a valid token ID (spec section 5).
token_claims_json: the exact JSON of TokenClaims as control state stores it (spec section 6.4); it parses and serializes back byte for byte.
revocations: the denylist of token and key entries refuses token, the first match in the order of spec section 8.1 (refused_by), or doesn't (null). Times are milliseconds.

principal_revocations: whether a principal revocation of revoked at control time before (milliseconds) refuses a token naming principal, signed by signer, issued at issued_at (milliseconds, or null when the token has no iat) (spec section 8.2).

signed_tokens: a token signed by a fixed Ed25519 key (RFC 8032 signatures are deterministic), byte for byte: the signing key is the 32-byte seed in hex, its key ID is kid, header and payload are the exact JSON of the first two parts, and token is the compact JWS. An issuer-signed case also gives the authority's seed and the issuer certificate, standard base64 of its DER, as x5c carries it. claims are the token's claims in the control state's JSON form (spec section 6.4). fleetringd's tests/tokens_vectors.rs checks this section; fleetring-control's tests check every other.

refused_tokens: a token every node refuses at now (milliseconds), verified for the fleet fleet against the one trusted authority whose 32-byte seed in hex is authority_seed, with an empty denylist; refused names why: malformed (spec section 6: a header field or claim that is null), x5c_encoding (section 6.2), kid_mismatch (section 7.1, check 1.6), issuer_certificate_expired (section 7.1, check 1.5), outlives_certificate or untrusted_root (section 7.1, check 4). The tokens were signed from the spec alone by an implementation independent of fleetringd's. fleetringd's tests/tokens_vectors.rs checks this section; fleetring-control's tests check every other.
